Mayor’s Fund Subcommittee Update
  • Member Jim Howat provided the update.
  • The Subcommittee reviewed and discussed the Wheeler Way application,
  staff will be requesting additional questions from the organization.
  • The subcommittee would like to receive reports back from those that are
  being funded, showcasing the work that they are doing.
  • City staff responded and said that the action had previously been approved
  and is currently a requirement in the application and listed in the MOU. GP
  Care Packages is the first to be required to submit a report back.
  • Anita Lakhani, Deputy City Attorney joins the meeting at 3:44pm.
Policy Subcommittee Update
  • Member Sarah Bedy provided the update.
  • The committee has been working on drafting the HSAC 2024-2025 policy
  recommendations for the last couple of subcommittee meetings.
  • The proposal includes policy recommendations to the Mayor and City
  Council, requesting that the City adopt focused sheltering goals made after a
  needs assessment is provided, prevention funding, and interim housing
  solutions.
  • Members discussed the four recommendations and requested feedback.
  • Members requested that the new strategic plan and HMIS data be leveraged
  for the recommendations. Discussions around quicker, less costly interim
  shelter operations and prevention programming arose.
  • The committee will meet next Monday and discuss a finished version of the
  draft.
Member Pam Chotiswatdi provided an update.
  • The CoC did not meet in March due to quorum issues.
  • There was a general meeting on 3/19/24.
  • No action was taken, the next Board meeting is April 9, 2024.
Public comment
 ⦁ Members of the public commented on the policy recommendations put forth by
the Policy Subcommittee.

A motion was made by Member Sngiem, seconded by Howat, to approve
recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

Yes:  7  Lie, Rew, Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Sngiem, Lewis
No:  0  None
Recused: 0  None
Abstain: 0  None
Absent: 2  Johnson, Simmons

3.  24-52830  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Multi-Service Center
  Services and Operations Staff Presentation.

  Tyler Ahtonen, Multi-Service Center Coordinator, presented in person.
  • The Multi-Service Center opened in 1999 and continues to serve as the
  primary access center for people experiencing homelessness. In 2023 the
  MSC had over 50,000 visits.
  • The MSC serves as the primary access center for people experiencing
  homelessness in Long Beach, with approximately 50,000 visits annually.
  • Services at the MSC include case management, medical clinic, mental
  health support, mail service, showers, and notary services.
  • Partnerships with various organizations provide additional support such as
  harm reduction, cell phone services, and veterinary care for pets of
  homeless individuals.
  • Members had questions regarding the collection of demographic data of
  MSC clients. There was a request from the members for more detailed data
  on monthly reports including the nature of visitors’ requests and responses
  received. Staff responded and identified foreseen challenges with securing
  detailed data. However, will review and will work with the HMIS team to
  provide quarterly reports that include more details.
  Paul Duncan, Homeless Services Bureau Manager, presented the Homeless
  Services Operation Report.
  • Detailed statistics on outreach and services provided in March, including
  requests, new enrollments, and services documented within HMIS.
  • Increase in first-time visitors to the multi-service center and average daily
  visits.
  • Introduction of phone line operators and their impact on call volume and
  case management.
  • Updates on shelter numbers and occupancy rates.
  • Announcement of staff retirements, promotions, and new hires within the
  department. Ongoing recruitment for various positions.
  • Progress update on data collection for the 2024 Point-In-Time Count.
  • Transition of referral and matching process for housing programs into the
  HMIS system. This includes increased training for staff and partners in the
  new system.
  • Increase in Measure H allocation to Long Beach COC/City for fiscal year 24-
  25.
  • A joint application for HHAP Round Five with coordination among various
  entities in the county was submitted.
  • Introduction of a new program by the county for locally funded encampment
  resolution programs. The transition of homeless individuals to long-term
  programs with a focus on functional zero homelessness in Signal Hill will
  later be an interim housing site prioritized for the Long Beach CoC.
  • There was a question and discussion regarding the Project Homekey site at

  1725 Long Beach Blvd and the release of the article that reported deaths at
  a city-owned building. Staff responded and clarified that the site is slated as
  interim housing for people experiencing homelessness who are most
  vulnerable, including the sick and elderly.
  • There were questions regarding an article about the Development Services
  Department’s oversight performance audit results from a city-owned building.
  Staff responded and shared that as it was not related to a Homeless
  Services Bureau audit, they could not answer on behalf of another City
  department.

  A motion was made by Vice Chair Rew, seconded by Howat, to approve

  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None

4.  24-52831  Recommendation to discuss the Chair and Vice Chair Report.

  • Vice-Chair Desiree Rew and Chair Julie Lie met for their monthly meeting.
  • Chair Julie Lie reminded members that Chair and Vice Chair elections are
  upcoming. Asked for a presentation from the ABC Shelter's operator voiced
  meeting location concerns and requested that meetings be kept to one
  location.
  • Staff responded, explaining challenges with finding the one location to
  accommodate reservations for months in advance. They shared that the
  HSB admin staff is expected to move into a new office that has a larger
  meeting room. They will begin to hold all Boards and Committees at that
  location.

  A motion was made by Howat, seconded by Member Bedy, to approve
  recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:
